analysis:
The Namami Gange mission was announced in the 2014 budget; Down To Earth reports it was described as aiming for a clean Ganga by 2019. Minister Uma Bharti said in 2015 the river would be among the cleanest by October 2018. Nitin Gadkari, who took over the ministry in September 2017, said in January 2019 the Ganga would be 100 per cent clean by March 2020 (earlier reports had him citing 70-80% by March 2019).

By April 2019, 98 of 298 sanctioned projects were complete and about a quarter of sanctioned funds spent. The deadline was later pushed to 2021 under minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.

In 2022-23, CPCB data showed dissolved oxygen and pH within limits but BOD above limits at 17 stations in 2022, and faecal coliform above the 2,500 MPN/100 ml limit at most stations in Bihar and West Bengal. Uttarakhand stations were within limits.
